neighbours.label: Insect and other invertebrate reproduction: ' eggs' being laid by insects, ' larvae' / ' larval' and the host plant they feed on; quiet for kitchen or bird eggs and for insects without the life cycle
fire: The moth deposits her eggs in clusters on the underside of oak leaves.
Nettles are the larval food plant of the small tortoiseshell butterfly.
After mating, the female wasp lays her eggs inside a living caterpillar.
Mosquitoes lay their eggs on still water, and the larvae hatch within days.
Wild fennel serves as a larval host for the swallowtail.
The weevil bores into the acorn and lays a single egg inside.
Fruit flies lay hundreds of eggs on rotting peaches in late summer.
The larvae of the stag beetle live in decaying wood for several years.
quiet: Beat three eggs with the milk and pour the mixture into a hot pan.
Nettles sting because tiny hairs on the leaves inject an irritant.
The wasp built a paper nest under the eaves of the shed.
Mosquitoes are most active at dusk near still water.
Wild fennel grows along the roadside and smells of aniseed.
The robin laid four blue eggs in a nest in the hedge.
Fruit flies gathered around the bowl of peaches on the table.
The stag beetle has huge jaws that look like antlers.

notes: Card: ' eggs' x7, ' larvae' x6, ' lar' x4, ' lay' x4, all butterflies, moths and mayflies. Probe: beetle 'lays her eggs' 0.65, 'larval host plant' 0.49, 'larvae feed' 0.22; cooking eggs 0.04, hen's eggs 0.02, salmon eggs 0.11, dragonflies hunting 0.04.
